## Objectives

- Learn why Java is a popular programming language.
- Manage multiple Java versions with SDKMAN!.
- Develop Java apps with IntelliJ IDEA and Maven.
- Manage dependencies with Maven.
- Develop essential skills for professional Java development.

# Java

## Java

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- General-purpose, object-oriented language.
- Write once, run anywhere (WORA).
- Created by James Gosling, 1995, at Sun Microsystems.
- The documentation seems scary; you will get used to it, and it is
  very useful.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/3/30/Java_programming_language_logo.svg){height="300"}
:::
:::

## Java virtual machine

- Source code is compiled to **bytecode**.
- The bytecode runs in the **Java virtual machine (JVM)**.
- Where a JVM exists, Java can run (most of the time).

## JVM versions

- Multiple implementations exist, targeting different platforms and
  features.
- **JDK** for development, **JRE** for running.
- **Eclipse Temurin** is the distribution we recommend and use.

## Java versions and version managers

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- **Java 25** is the latest LTS: the version of this course.
- [SDKMAN!](https://sdkman.io/) manages multiple Java versions (you
  installed it in chapter 00).
- Match versions within a project for consistency.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://sdkman.io/assets/img/sdk-man-small-pattern.svg){width="70%"}
:::
:::

## Compiling and running Java programs (1/3)

Given the following `HelloWorld.java` file:

```java
public class HelloWorld {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        String message = "Hello, World!";

        System.out.println(message);
    }
}
```

## Compiling and running Java programs (2/3)

Compile manually with the `javac` command:

```sh
javac HelloWorld.java
```

Execute with the `java` command:

```sh
java HelloWorld
```

## Compiling and running Java programs (3/3)

Modern way: package into a **JAR** file with Maven, run with `java -jar`:

```sh
java -Xmx1024M -Xms1024M -jar minecraft_server.1.21.jar nogui
```

(Yes, the Minecraft server is a JAR file.)

## Garbage collection

- Java has automatic memory management: no manual `malloc`/`free` as in
  C or C++.
- The **garbage collector** ("GC") runs periodically to free memory.
- An object is eligible when it is no longer referenced (out of scope or
  `null`).

## Summary: Java

- General-purpose, class-based, object-oriented language.
- Compiled to bytecode, executed by the JVM; portable by design.
- Versions evolve; LTS releases matter (Java 25 today).
- Version managers (SDKMAN!) install and switch between versions.

# IntelliJ IDEA

## IntelliJ IDEA

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- IDE for (Java) software development.
- Developed by JetBrains.
- Works on Windows, macOS, Linux.
- Quite a standard in the industry.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://resources.jetbrains.com/storage/products/company/brand/logos/IntelliJ_IDEA_icon.svg){width="60%"}
:::
:::

## Community Edition and Ultimate Edition

- **Community** (free) and **Ultimate** (paid).
- Free student license available; get it with your HEIG-VD email.
- The Community Edition is sufficient for this course.

## JetBrains Toolbox App

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- Manages multiple JetBrains IDEs.
- Install and update in one place.
- Optional but very useful.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://resources.jetbrains.com/storage/products/company/brand/logos/Toolbox_icon.svg){width="60%"}
:::
:::

## Configuration files and Git

- IntelliJ creates a `.idea` directory with the project configuration.
- It allows sharing project settings between developers.
- Some of its files contain **local** configuration and must be ignored
  in Git; chapter 03 shows what to keep.

## Summary: IntelliJ IDEA

- The reference IDE for Java development.
- Community Edition is enough; the student license unlocks Ultimate.
- The `.idea` directory is shared, except its local parts
  (`.gitignore`).

# Maven

## Maven

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
- Maintained by the Apache Software Foundation.
- Software project management tool.
- Manages **dependencies**.
- **Build automation** tool.
- Defines a standard project structure.
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/52/Apache_Maven_logo.svg)
:::
:::

## Maven project structure

Standardized directory structure; conventions simplify the build:

```text
my-project/
├── pom.xml
└── src/
    ├── main/
    │   ├── java/          # application sources
    │   └── resources/     # config files, assets
    └── test/
        └── java/          # unit tests
```

## The `pom.xml` file

Configuration and build settings, shared among developers:

```xml
<project>
  <groupId>ch.heigvd.dai</groupId>
  <artifactId>my-project</artifactId>
  <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>          <!-- external library -->
      <groupId>info.picocli</groupId>
      <artifactId>picocli</artifactId>
      <version>4.7.7</version>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>
</project>
```

## Maven lifecycle

- Maven defines the build process, composed of **phases** loading
  plugin **goals**.
- The phases you will use daily:
  - `compile`: compile the sources.
  - `test`: run the unit tests.
  - `package`: build the JAR.
  - `clean`: remove build outputs (`target/`).

## Maven Repository

- [Maven Central](https://central.sonatype.com/): public repository of
  Java libraries.
- Maven downloads dependencies automatically.
- You can publish your own libraries.
- Many libraries available, such as
  [picocli](https://picocli.info/), for building CLI applications.

## Maven wrapper

- Use Maven without installing it: the wrapper script downloads it.
- Ensures a consistent Maven version across the team.
- Use `./mvnw` (or `mvnw.cmd` on Windows) instead of `mvn`.

## Summary: Maven

- Project management, dependency manager and build tool in one.
- Standard directory structure and standard build process.
- The `pom.xml` file is the single source of project configuration.

## What will you do?

- Create a Maven project in IntelliJ IDEA.
- Build and run a small CLI application with

- Publish the project on GitHub, with signed commits.

**Do not hesitate to help each other! There's no need to rush!**
